articles.title: Mermaid Inn Restaurateurs Ink 2K SF at 61 West 74th Street for New Eatery
articles.narrative: Restaurateurs Danny Abrams and Cindy Smith, co-founders of Mermaid Inn, have signed a 2,300-square-foot lease for a new, as-yet-unnamed restaurant concept at 61 West 74th Street in New York City. The space, which includes a basement, was secured at an annual rental rate of $130 per square foot. This new venture expands their presence in the Upper West Side, building on the success of their nearby Mermaid Inn location.

data_points.address: 61 West 74th Street, New York City, NY
data_points.project_notes: The site previously housed Patsy's Pizzeria, which closed in January 2026.

articles.title: Nordstrom Rack Takes 22K SF in Wellington, Fla.
articles.narrative: Nordstrom Rack has signed a 22,000-square-foot lease at The Shoppes at Isla Verde in Wellington, FL, with an anticipated opening in spring 2027. The discount retailer will occupy space in the MetLife Investment Management-owned shopping center, which is managed by Urban Retail Properties. This new lease fills a vacancy left by a previous tenant, contributing to the center's evolving tenant mix.

data_points.project_notes: The 207,000-square-foot shopping center was previously acquired by MetLife in 2018 for $73.75 million. The space was formerly occupied by a fabric retailer that closed in 2025.

articles.title: Immigration Law Firm Manifest Law Subleases 18K SF at 902 Broadway
articles.narrative: Manifest Law, an immigration law firm, has subleased 18,200 square feet on the entire eighth floor at 902 Broadway in New York City. The firm is taking over space previously occupied by Adaptive Security, which recently subleased larger premises elsewhere. This move highlights the Union Square and Flatiron districts' appeal for growing companies seeking collaborative office environments.

data_points.notable_features: Located between the Flatiron Building and Union Square.
data_points.project_notes: Manifest Law is relocating from 333 Park Avenue South. Adaptive Security previously occupied this space and subleased 51,220 square feet from BarkBox at 120 Broadway.

articles.title: Starwood’s Net Income Drops 95% Annually — and Then Its Stock Drops
articles.narrative: Starwood Property Trust reported a significant 95% year-over-year decline in net income for Q2 2026, leading to a 4% drop in its stock price. Despite this, Chairman and CEO Barry Sternlicht expressed confidence in the firm's fundamentals, citing improving conditions across most U.S. and European asset classes, particularly in multifamily, self-storage, senior housing, and logistics. The firm's president, Jeffrey DiModica, highlighted a near-record $6.7 billion in year-to-date deployment and strong loan origination, though he acknowledged some multifamily assets in Sun Belt markets faced downgrades due to elevated supply and higher rates. Sternlicht remains optimistic about the firm's ability to restore earnings power and maximize shareholder value by addressing underperforming assets.

articles.title: AI Employee Management Platform Warp Triples Footprint at 156 Fifth Avenue
articles.narrative: Warp, an AI-driven employee management platform, has significantly expanded its office footprint at 156 Fifth Avenue in New York City's Flatiron District. The company secured an additional 16,500 square feet, bringing its total occupancy to 24,500 square feet across the seventh and eighth floors. This expansion, less than a year after its initial lease in the building, reflects the rapid growth of AI companies and their substantial demand for office space in the city.

data_points.address: 156 Fifth Avenue, New York City, NY
data_points.notable_features: Building is now 100% occupied. Landlord made upgrades to the seventh floor and opened a new amenity space on the third floor.
data_points.project_notes: Warp's initial lease in Fall 2025 was for 8,000 square feet on the eighth floor. This expansion brings their total footprint to 24,500 square feet.

articles.market_intelligence: The New York City AI industry is experiencing uniquely rapid office growth, with companies tripling and quadrupling their footprints rather than incremental expansion.

articles.title: Stena Real Estate to Renovate 580,558 SF Office Campus in Houston’s Energy Corridor
articles.narrative: Stena Real Estate AB, the American ownership arm of Swedish investment company Stena Property, is undertaking a significant renovation of Woodbranch Plaza, a four-building, 580,558-square-foot office campus in Houston's Energy Corridor. The capital improvement program will focus on upgrading the lobby, common areas, and restrooms, activating new shared amenity spaces, and enhancing outdoor landscaping. Additionally, Stena is constructing speculative office suites to attract new tenants.

data_points.notable_features: Four-building campus with existing fitness center, conference facilities, and a deli. Upgrades include new shared amenity spaces, lobby, common areas, restrooms, and enhanced landscaping.
data_points.project_notes: Renovation and construction of speculative office suites.

articles.title: Newmark Brokers Sale of 376,259 SF Office Campus in North Dallas
articles.narrative: Newmark has brokered the sale of Tollway Plaza, a 376,259-square-foot office campus in North Dallas. The campus, consisting of two eight-story buildings, was 91 percent leased at the time of sale with a weighted average remaining lease term of 5.5 years. Newmark also arranged acquisition financing for the buyer, a partnership led by Tourmaline Capital Partners.

articles.title: Foundry Commercial Underway on 13-Acre IOS Facility in Hutchins, Texas
articles.narrative: Foundry Commercial is developing Wintergreen Gardens, a 13-acre industrial outdoor storage (IOS) facility in Hutchins, Texas. The project, which began construction earlier this summer, will feature 9 acres of concrete-paved outdoor storage and two industrial buildings totaling 25,000 square feet, with delivery expected in the first quarter of 2027.

data_points.notable_features: Features 9 acres of concrete-paved outdoor storage space.

articles.title: Lee & Associates Negotiates 26,600 SF Industrial Lease in Northwest Dallas
articles.narrative: Lee & Associates has brokered a 26,600-square-foot industrial lease in northwest Dallas. The transaction involved Brookfield Asset Management as the landlord and an entity operating as Render Collective LLC as the tenant.

articles.title: JLL Brokers $147M Sale of Seniors Housing Portfolio in Metro Atlanta
articles.narrative: JLL's National Seniors Housing Capital Markets team has brokered the sale of a five-property seniors housing portfolio located in various submarkets north of Atlanta. The portfolio, comprising 611 units and 701 beds across assisted living and memory care facilities, was acquired by an institutional investor in an all-cash transaction. The seller was a joint venture between Centric Development and Sage Equities, which developed the properties between 2018 and 2022. Claiborne Senior Living has been retained by the new owner to continue managing the communities.

data_points.notable_features: Portfolio includes assisted living and memory care facilities with amenities such as theaters, restaurant-style dining, bistros, bars, art studios, game rooms, and landscaped courtyards.

articles.title: Rosemont’s Conor Commercial Real Estate names vice president of development
Buffalo Grove’s PREMIER Design + Build adds executive vice president
articles.narrative: PREMIER Design + Build Group, a Buffalo Grove, Illinois-based firm, has appointed Ed Pitula as Executive Vice President. In this role, Pitula will be responsible for overseeing operations and strategic growth within PREMIER's Central Region, focusing on strengthening client relationships and expanding the company's market presence. He brings over 30 years of experience in development and construction, having delivered more than 12.7 million square feet of commercial real estate across various sectors.

articles.title: Indianapolis’ Premier Commercial Real Estate Services adds associate broker
articles.narrative: Premier Commercial Real Estate Services, an Indianapolis-based firm, has expanded its brokerage division by appointing Andrew Klink as an Associate Broker. This move is part of the firm's strategy to cultivate new talent and enhance its service capabilities across Indiana and surrounding regions. Klink, a former intern, will gain experience in various commercial real estate services, including landlord and tenant representation, investment sales, and site selection, under the mentorship of senior brokers.

articles.title: NAI Ruhl Commercial Company closes sale of former Quad-City Times headquarters in Davenport
articles.narrative: The former Quad-City Times headquarters in Davenport, IA, a 122,800-square-foot landmark property, has been sold to The Geifman Group. The buyer plans extensive remodeling to convert the facility into a multi-tenant building. The property, which includes office and high-bay production space, was exclusively brokered by NAI Ruhl Commercial Company.

data_points.notable_features: Overlooks the Mississippi River; includes two-story office space and high-bay production/warehouse space.

articles.title: Marcus & Millichap closes $3.55 million sale of retail property in Sussex
articles.narrative: Marcus & Millichap has brokered the sale of Sussex Gateway Retail Center, a nine-suite retail property in Sussex, Wisconsin, for $3.55 million. The property consists of two multi-tenant retail buildings totaling approximately 24,834 square feet. The center benefits from high traffic counts and excellent visibility due to its location across from major retailers.

data_points.notable_features: Anchored by a national discount retailer, with strong tenant mix and positioned across from a major grocery store and convenience store.

articles.title: The New Role of Transitional Debt in Commercial Real Estate Finance
articles.narrative: A new report from Nuveen highlights the evolving role of transitional debt in commercial real estate finance, noting its shift from a temporary solution to a core strategy for life insurers. This change is driven by banks reducing their CRE lending exposure due to tighter regulations and lower property valuations. Private credit funds and life insurance companies are increasingly filling this void, providing capital to bridge the gap between traditional mortgages and opportunistic debt. Nuveen identifies three key structural shifts: banks transitioning to warehouse financing roles, a reset in property values leading to more realistic pricing and durable risk-return profiles for loans, and a significant wave of loan maturities between 2025 and 2027 creating a steady pipeline for transitional lenders.

articles.title: The Forces Impacting CRE as AI, Energy and Supply Constraints Take Hold
articles.narrative: JLL's mid-year "Global Real Estate Outlook" report highlights six structural forces reshaping international commercial real estate markets, revising an earlier optimistic 2026 forecast due to geopolitical conflicts and trade tensions. The report emphasizes that cost management has become a primary business driver, with supply constraints creating opportunities for retrofitting existing properties. It also notes the increasing importance of building quality, amenities, and AI-enabled features in occupier decisions, as artificial intelligence transitions from experimentation to operational impact, potentially altering office demand. Furthermore, energy security is now a critical factor in development and leasing, while private capital is expanding its role in CRE investment amid improving pricing clarity and a competitive debt market.

articles.title: Q2: U.S. Industrial Market Moves Toward Balance as Demand Outpaces New Supply
articles.narrative: The U.S. industrial market is showing signs of stabilization in Q2 2026, with demand beginning to outpace new deliveries and developers exercising discipline in adding new supply. The national industrial vacancy rate has stabilized after increasing for several quarters, driven by increased demand for larger warehouse and distribution facilities. This shift suggests the market is moving beyond recent oversupply concerns and closer to equilibrium, with absorption now exceeding new deliveries.
articles.market_intelligence: The national industrial vacancy rate stabilized in Q2 2026 after steadily increasing for several quarters, declining from its late 2024 peak. Industrial demand outpaced new deliveries for the first time in several quarters. Third-party logistics providers were the largest source of industrial leasing activity in the first half of 2026, with manufacturers also contributing to demand growth. Leasing from general retailers and wholesalers declined. Much of the space under construction consists of build-to-suit projects and larger speculative developments of 200,000 square feet or more.

articles.title: Fintech Firm More Than Doubles Footprint at 10 Astor Place
articles.narrative: Fintech firm Maybern has significantly expanded its presence at 10 Astor Place in New York City, more than doubling its office footprint from 11,000 square feet to 30,000 square feet. The long-term lease expansion, which includes the entire fourth floor, demonstrates the tenant's strong confidence in the boutique building and its offerings. The landlord noted that such expansions by existing tenants are a powerful indicator of a property's value, particularly for buildings that offer enduring architecture and character.

data_points.address: 10 Astor Place, New York City, NY
data_points.notable_features: Boutique building with enduring architecture and character.
data_points.project_notes: Maybern originally relocated to the property in 2024.

articles.title: Production Fabrication Firm Relocates to Rancho Dominguez
articles.narrative: Cactus Fabrication, a production fabrication firm for the entertainment industry, has signed a 10-year lease for a 35,333-square-foot industrial property in Rancho Dominguez, CA. The company is relocating from a smaller Los Angeles facility to accommodate its expanding operations. The property's large footprint, heavy electrical capacity, functional layout, and recent modernization were key factors in the relocation, providing a best-in-class asset suitable for attracting employees and impressing clients.

data_points.address: 2945 East Maria St., Rancho Dominguez, CA
data_points.notable_features: Features heavy electrical capacity, a large secured side yard, and a separate front-loading area. The building has been recently modernized with superior office space.
data_points.project_notes: Tenant is relocating from a smaller property in Los Angeles.

articles.title: Investors Want A Slice Of Exclusive Florida Keys Hotel Market
articles.narrative: The Florida Keys hotel market is experiencing a surge in investor interest, driven by a significant increase in leisure travel to the region. This heightened demand is reflected in recent major sales and investments, indicating a booming market for hospitality assets in the Keys.

articles.title: CRE’s ESG Retreat Masks Growing Spending On Climate Risk
articles.narrative: The commercial real estate industry is increasingly prioritizing climate risk data and predictive models, even as the broader focus on ESG investing appears to be diminishing. This shift reflects a growing recognition that understanding and mitigating climate-related physical and transition risks is crucial for asset valuation, investment decisions, and long-term portfolio resilience. The demand for sophisticated data tools to assess these risks is rising, indicating a strategic pivot towards tangible risk management rather than solely broad ESG mandates.

articles.title: Portman's Ten Twenty Spring Nabs Refinancing: The Atlanta Deal Sheet
articles.narrative: Portman has secured a $278 million refinancing package for its Ten Twenty Spring tower in Atlanta, a prominent office building that houses a strong tenant mix. This refinancing deal underscores the continued institutional interest in well-located, high-quality office assets in the Atlanta market.

articles.title: OPI Sells Vacant Philly Office Building For $42M
articles.narrative: A real estate investment trust has sold its sole office property in Philadelphia, a 441,000-square-foot vacant building, to the city for $42 million. The transaction marks the disposition of the REIT's last office asset in the market.

articles.title: Faneuil Hall Owner J. Safra Group Sues Tenants, Alleging $2M In Unpaid Rent
articles.narrative: J. Safra Group, the owner of Faneuil Hall Marketplace, has filed a lawsuit against seven tenants, seeking $2 million in alleged unpaid rent. The legal action highlights ongoing challenges in commercial property management and tenant relations, particularly concerning rent obligations.
